contract: Clip double-click in Session/Arrangement, Selector, Toggle or Ctrl+Alt+3 Win/Cmd+Option+3 Mac opens Clip View. Toggle while Device View is open stacks Clip View above it. Dragging top border resizes; bottom closes it.
Clip View opens in focused window and displays current clip even when selected in other window. F12 moves view between windows; Shift+Tab does so only when Use Tab Key to Navigate is off.
Clip Activator off deactivates clip playback in Session launch or Arrangement timeline; context Deactivate/0 also available. Multi-selection off deactivates all selected clips.

Clip Rename and Edit Info Text are available through specified title/Edit/clip menus. Audio clip rename does not rename source sample. Multi-selection shows count; common new name is not displayed as title.

New clips inherit track color; palette changes clip color. Track/group Assign Color commands affect clips only in the invoking Session or Arrangement view. Multi-selection title is striped while individual selected clips accept color.

Title plus panels/editor are shared layout. Main/Extended properties are common; audio adds Audio Utilities/Transform, MIDI adds Pitch-Time/Transform/Generate. Editors and additional properties depend on clip type.
Panels support horizontal, vertical or automatic arrangement through border drag/View menu/title context. Arrangement is remembered on future opening. Title double-click/Fold minimizes panels.
Audio editor modes are Sample/Envelope; MIDI modes Notes/Envelope/MPE. Tabs/View commands or Alt+Tab Win/Option+Tab Mac switch modes.
Start/End value fields define unlooped playing region. Warped audio displays bars-beats-sixteenths; unwarped displays minutes-seconds-milliseconds.
Set Start/End during playback take current playhead position according to global quantization; exact rounding/ties/dispatch are unspecified here.
Loop Position/Length and Loop toggle define repeat region; initial Loop Length is described as total clip length. Audio loop is unavailable until Warp on; unwarped audio cannot loop.

Set Loop Position moves start to current playhead rounded by global quantization and enables loop; Set Loop Length then moves end to current position. With loop off, Set Length ends loop at current position preserving preset length and enables it.
Set buttons, Loop toggle, loop region and Start/End positions are eligible MIDI mapping targets; actual controller mapping/takeover belongs to MIDI user mapping.
Clip time signature is per-clip display state, independent from project meter and does not change clip playback.
Scale button/root/name are clip properties. Audio scale forwards to scale-aware devices rather than altering raw clip playback; MIDI piano highlighting and scale edits belong to MIDI owner.

Extended panel shows launch controls for Session clips only. Arrangement audio has no Extended panel; Arrangement MIDI has MIDI bank/program only. Full launch and Follow Actions remain with clip-launch and future Session packet.

MIDI bank/sub-bank/program selectors support documented 128 choices each and send on clip launch to supporting targets. Dash leaves corresponding message unset. MIDI bytes, value numbering and target support remain U.
Warp off plays sample at original tempo irrespective of Set tempo; Warp on follows Set tempo when metrical structure is valid. Preparation/analysis and Warp algorithms remain with their owners.

Reverse creates a new reversed sample and repoints clip, applying clip settings under documented transformation rules. Before save it resides in Temporary Folder; after Set save under Project Samples/Processed/Reverse.
On reverse, Warp Markers and region/loop positions are reflected with sample material; clip envelopes keep timeline positions. Exact endpoint/frame/marker transformation is not specified.

Long reversal may show progress and temporarily lock further actions while existing clips continue. When waveform generation begins, other actions/playback become available. Reverse pair is cached until application closes; no duration deadline or glitch-free guarantee.
Session cannot reverse multiple clips together. Arrangement time-range Reverse Clip(s)/R is owned by Arrangement editing, whose MIDI-containing selection limitation remains applicable.

Edit opens configured external sample editor; Live playback must stop before external processing. Return uses edited version; Warp Markers retained only when sample length unchanged. Shared source edits can affect other referencing clips.

Clip Fade toggle is Session-only; Arrangement uses fade envelopes. Manual describes signal-dependent 0-4 ms edge fades and new-clip default on when Create Fades on Clip Edges enabled. Exact fade kernel remains with playback/Arrangement owners.
RAM toggle requests referenced audio in memory rather than realtime disk reads; capacity/resource/disk-overload observations in prose are not a memory guarantee or benchmark.
Hi-Q toggles higher-quality rate conversion with described CPU tradeoff. Approximate 19-semitone audibility prose supplies no spectral/CPU metric or universal threshold.
Audio Gain uses dB; Pitch semitone knob/field and separate cents field are distinct, with 100 cents per semitone. Multi-selected differing gains display split triangle handles.

Audio Transform panel offers Quantize for warped clips using current grid or specified meter and Amount; audio has no Generate panel. Marker movement/selection/rounding stays with Warp owner/future Warp workflow packet.
Editor time-ruler vertical drag zooms and horizontal drag scrolls; wheel/trackpad scrolls. Behavior is shared by Sample and MIDI editors.
Z/Zoom to Clip Selection zooms current time selection; X returns one zoom state per press, including repeated Z history.

Selector overview spans clip Start-End; outline represents visible editor portion and dragging scrolls/zooms. Follow scrolls with playhead, pauses for editor edits and resumes after stop/restart or click in scrub area. MIDI-specific editor Follow stays with MIDI owner.
Start/End markers drag or move with left/right arrows; Alt Win/Option Mac plus arrows on either selected marker moves whole region.
Permanent Scrub Areas on permits click in lower waveform or scrub area to jump playback; off permits Shift-click in scrub area or beat-time ruler.

Scrub jumps use global quantization; holding left button repeats a portion the size of selected quantization, with small/None allowing scrubbing. Chase MIDI Notes routes to playback-core note/chase gaps; no repeated-note oracle is supplied here.
Loop brace handles edit start/end; brace drag moves it. Left/right nudges grid, up/down shifts by length; Ctrl Win/Cmd Mac left/right resizes by grid, up/down doubles/halves length.
Clip begins at start marker regardless of loop brace, allowing initial material to run into a later loop.
Sample header displays name/rate/depth/channel count. Multi-selection shows sample count and asterisk for differing properties. Name click/Show in Browser reveals source.
Unlooped Crop Clip Sample uses Start-End; looped cropping begins at earlier Start/Loop Start and ends at Loop End.
Time selection exposes Crop Clip Sample to Time Selection; Ctrl+Shift+J Win/Cmd+Shift+J Mac triggers applicable crop command.
Audio crop creates a new shorter sample, temporarily in configured Temporary Folder and after save in Project Samples/Processed/Crop.
Browser drag to Clip View or selected browser sample double-click/Enter replaces referenced sample. Pitch/volume settings remain; Warp Markers retained only for exact same source length.

Show Similar Files opens similarity search; Manage Sample File opens Set File Manager with current source selected. File Manager replacements/destructive edits can affect all clips/instruments sharing source.
Drag from empty clip slot or Ctrl Win/Cmd Mac/Shift extends clip multi-selection. Visible properties generally include only common properties of selected contents.
Mixed-value multi-selection shows a value range. Dragging control to absolute maximum/minimum makes selected settings identical and subsequently adjustable as one.

Clip Update Rate in Record/Warp/Launch settings quantizes changes to a running clip. Launch Mode/Warp Mode can be defaults for new clips. Complete affected-control set, rate choices and precedence versus global launch quantization are U.
Save Default Clip button is audio-specific and supports multi-selected samples; its ASD/new-import/nonretroactive semantics are owned by REQ-MEDIA-FILE-010, distinct from Live Clip devices.
Required region/loop input bounds and error outcomes remain unknown.
Required ordering between edits, scrub, launch and transport remains unknown.
Required edit/processed-file undo/redo transactions remain unknown.
Required save/reopen/default/processed-file state remains unknown.
Required cancellation/progress/error outcomes remain unknown.
Required clip/view/Set teardown and concurrent-selection outcomes remain unknown.
Required numerical audio and media-boundary oracles remain unknown.
Required multi-selection/common-value/context outcomes remain unknown.
